contentHtml:
How long to cook sausage in air fryer? Just 10 to 15 minutes is all it takes to get them golden and juicy! Why air fry your sausages? It’s the quickest and cleanest way to achieve perfectly crispy sausages with juicy interiors. Whether you’re prepping breakfast or whipping up a quick snack, knowing these times can transform your meals.

Cooking sausages in an air fryer is incredibly efficient and simple. This method not only saves time but also reduces mess, ensuring you get perfectly cooked sausages with minimal effort. It’s ideal for busy mornings or quick, tasty dinners.

In this article, you will learn:

  • How to adjust cooking times based on sausage type
  • Tips to ensure your sausages cook evenly
  • The best ways to serve and enjoy your air-fried sausages

With these quick steps, you’ll master the art of cooking sausages in an air fryer in no time!

Essential Equipment

To start air frying sausages like a pro, you’ll need just a few key pieces of equipment. Here’s what to gather before you begin:

  1. Air Fryer: Choose a model that fits your kitchen size and cooking needs. Larger air fryers are great for big batches, while compact models are perfect for smaller meals or kitchens.
  2. Tongs: A good pair of tongs will help you safely turn your sausages midway through cooking to ensure they brown evenly.
  3. Meat Thermometer: This isn’t mandatory, but if you want to be extra sure your sausages are cooked through, a meat thermometer can give you peace of mind.

By having these items ready, you'll make the cooking process smoother and ensure that your sausages come out perfectly every time.

Types of Sausages You Can Air Fry

Air frying is versatile enough to handle all sorts of sausages, from fresh to frozen, and even special varieties. Discover how long to cook sausage in air fryer with this quick guide to what you can cook:

  1. Fresh Sausages: These include your typical pork, beef, or chicken sausages. They usually take about 10-15 minutes at 180°C (360°F), turning halfway through.
  2. Frozen Sausages: No need to thaw; you can air fry them directly. They'll need about 15-20 minutes at the same temperature, also turned halfway through.
  3. Vegan Sausages: These are becoming increasingly popular and can also be air fried. They typically require slightly less time, around 8-12 minutes.
  4. Special Varieties:
    • Chicken Sausages: Lighter and often leaner, needing about 10 minutes.
    • Wild Boar Sausages: Richer and denser, usually take about 15-20 minutes.
    • Smoked Sausages: Already cooked, these just need warming through for about 5-7 minutes.

Knowing the type of sausage and adjusting the cooking time accordingly ensures perfect results every time.

Preparation Guide

Preparing your sausages for the air fryer is straightforward, but a few key steps can enhance the flavour and ensure even cooking:

  1. Poking Holes: Gently prick fresh sausages with a fork before cooking. This helps release fats and juices, preventing them from bursting and helping them cook evenly.
  2. Spacing: Make sure to place the sausages in the air fryer basket in a single layer with space between them. This allows the hot air to circulate freely, ensuring that each sausage cooks thoroughly and gets a nice crisp skin.
  3. No Oil Needed: Unlike traditional methods, you don’t need to add oil to your sausages when air frying. The natural fats are enough to achieve that desired crispiness.
  4. Preheating Your Air Fryer: For the best results, preheat your air fryer for about 3-5 minutes at the cooking temperature before adding your sausages. This helps start the cooking process off strong for a perfect finish.

Cooking Instructions

Cooking sausages in an air fryer is not only quick but also very straightforward. Here's how to ensure they come out perfectly whenever you know how long to cook sausages in air fryer.

  1. Preheat Your Air Fryer: Start by preheating your air fryer to 180°C (360°F) for about 3-5 minutes. This ensures your sausages start cooking immediately at the right temperature.
  2. Place the Sausages: Arrange your sausages in a single layer in the air fryer basket. Remember not to overcrowd them to allow for even cooking.
  3. Cooking Time:
    • For fresh sausages, cook for 10-15 minutes.
    • For frozen sausages, cook for 15-20 minutes.
    • For special varieties (like chicken or vegan sausages), adjust times as necessary, usually a bit shorter than pork.
    • Always turn the sausages halfway through the cooking time to ensure they brown evenly on all sides.
  4. Check Doneness: For the best results, the internal temperature of the sausages should reach 160°F (71°C) when checked with a meat thermometer.
  5. Rest Before Serving: Once cooked, let the sausages rest for a few minutes in the air fryer before serving. This helps the juices redistribute, making your sausages even more flavorful and juicy.

Variations and Substitutions

Air-frying sausages are flexible, allowing you to experiment with different flavours and adaptations based on dietary preferences or what you have on hand. Here are some ideas:

  1. Seasoning Variations:
    • Spicy: Add a sprinkle of chilli flakes or cayenne pepper before cooking for a kick.
    • Herby: Toss with dried herbs like rosemary, thyme, or oregano for a classic flavour.
    • Sweet and Savory: A light brush of maple syrup or honey five minutes before they're done adds a delightful glaze.
  2. Meat Substitutions:
    • If you're avoiding pork, try chicken, turkey, or beef sausages.
    • For a vegetarian option, many brands offer delicious vegan sausages that are great in the air fryer.
  3. Dietary Adjustments:
    • Gluten-Free: Check labels to ensure the sausages and any added seasonings are gluten-free.
    • Low-Fat: Opt for sausages with a lower fat content, like chicken or turkey, which still turn out wonderfully in the air fryer.
  4. International Flavors:
    • Italian Style: Mix in some fennel seeds and garlic powder.
    • German Style: Serve with sauerkraut and mustard on the side.

Serving Suggestions

Once your sausages are beautifully cooked and ready, pairing them with the right sides and condiments can turn a simple meal into a feast. Here are some serving suggestions to enhance your air-fried sausages:

  1. Classic Breakfast: Serve air-fried sausages with scrambled eggs, toast, and grilled tomatoes for a hearty breakfast.
  2. Sausage Sandwich: Slice the sausages into a crusty baguette, add caramelized onions, a smear of mustard, and if you like, some peppery arugula.
  3. With Vegetables: Air fry some peppers and onions in the same basket during the last few minutes of cooking for a delicious and colourful accompaniment.
  4. Pasta Night: Slice cooked sausages and toss them into your favourite pasta sauce. Serve over spaghetti or penne for a satisfying meal.
  5. Sausage and Potato Dinner: Cube some potatoes and season them with herbs. Air fry alongside the sausages for a complete meal.
  6. As a Pizza Topping: Slice the sausages thinly and spread them over your pizza base before baking for extra flavour.

Storage and Reheating Tips

Proper storage and reheating are crucial for enjoying your air-fried sausages even after the initial meal. Here’s how to do it right:

  1. Storing Leftovers:
    • Cool Completely: Allow sausages to cool to room temperature before storing to prevent condensation that could make them soggy.
    • Refrigerate: Place the sausages in an airtight container and refrigerate for up to three days.
    • Freeze for Longer Storage: If you won’t be eating them within a few days, wrap the sausages tightly in plastic wrap or place them in a freezer bag. They can be frozen for up to two months.
  2. Reheating:
    • Air Fryer: Reheat leftovers in the air fryer at 160°C (320°F) for 4-5 minutes, or until they are hot and crispy again.
    • Oven: You can also reheat them in the oven at a similar temperature until they are thoroughly warmed.
  3. Safety Tips:
    • Never Refreeze Thawed Sausages: If you’ve thawed the sausages in the refrigerator, do not refreeze them. Cook and eat them within the safe storage period.
    • Check Temperature: Ensure that reheated sausages reach an internal temperature of at least 74°C (165°F) to ensure they are safe to eat.

FAQs

Here are answers to some of the most frequently asked questions about air frying sausages:

Can you cook smoked sausage in the air fryer?

Yes, you can cook smoked sausage in the air fryer. It typically takes about 5-7 minutes since they are already cooked and you just need to heat them through.

How long to cook already smoked sausage?

Already smoked sausage should be heated for about 5-7 minutes in the air fryer at 180°C (360°F).

How long to put sausages in the air fryer?

For fresh sausages, air fry them for 10-15 minutes. For frozen sausages, 15-20 minutes is ideal.

Can you cook sausages in an air fryer at 200 degrees?

Yes, cooking at 200°C (about 390°F) can work, but it will decrease the cooking time and may require more frequent checking to prevent overcooking.

What temperature to cook smoked sausage in air fryer?

Cook smoked sausage at 180°C (360°F) to heat it thoroughly without drying it out.

How long to cook various types of sausage in the air fryer?

Italian sausage: 10-12 minutes

Polish sausage: 10-12 minutes

Chicken sausage: 8-10 minutes

Frozen sausage: 15-20 minutes

Smoked sausage: 5-7 minutes

Breakfast sausages: 8-10 minutes

Conclusion

Cooking sausages in an air fryer is not only quick and easy but also results in delicious, evenly cooked sausages every time. You can ensure perfect results by following the specific cooking times and temperatures provided for various types of sausages, from fresh to frozen and even special varieties like chicken and smoked. With the right equipment and preparation methods, your air fryer can become your go-to tool for making sausages.
